This is f*cking gold..

Chinese researchers just released a paper with a brutal title: "The End of Prediction".

The case is simple: an AI that outputs BUY or SELL is finished as a product.

Any signal a model can read is priced in before it finishes reading, and active managers already lose to the index over any multi-year window.

The question a model answers well is different: what changed, and what is the evidence that it is real rather than noise.

So the architecture flips. Plain code finds the anomaly, a million-token model compares eight quarters in one pass, and the heavy reasoning model is spent only on arguing against the result.

10,000 companies a day become 40 deep reads and 8 reasoning passes -- about $450 of inference where a naive full pass costs $60,000.

Flagged events hit 37% precision against a 15 to 20% base rate. A real edge, and still nowhere near a forecast.

The output has no score and no call. Only what changed, sourced, and what contradicts it.

That is exactly the pipeline I built and wrote up below: Robinhood data, Kimi K3 for the reading, GPT-6 Astra for the counter-thesis.

The entire paper in one line: you are selling research velocity, not prediction ↓

hits.text:
This is f*cking insane..

Chinese researchers just released a paper with a brutal title: "The End of Copy Trading".

The case is simple: the wallet you have been copying might be a bot, and nothing in a leaderboard will tell you.

A leaderboard shows returns. It does not show whether the wallet is a person, a script, or one of ten wallets that entered the same coin in the same second.

So they read Solana and Robinhood Chain straight from public nodes and typed every big buyer at block time: sniper, flipper, accumulator, whale or bot.

Three or more wallets into one coin within seconds is a pack, scored for coordination. In one live session a pack entered DUES in one second at 72% coordinated -- near-identical buy sizes, wallets never seen together before.

Five on-chain checks -- concentration, wash trades, pack buying, early dumping, copycat name -- collapse into one scam score from 0 to 100.

No wallet connect, no keys, nothing stored. The only thing that touches a model is the judgment call, and only when you click.

That is exactly the tracker I built and shipped for free below: it is called WolfBrain, and the first thing to do is paste the wallet you have been copying into Wolf DNA.

The entire paper in one line: look before you ape ↓

hits.name: wast3
hits.text:
Anthropic went looking three kilometres down and pulled out a protein that gets stronger under pressure that flattens every enzyme we build.

It was never asked to invent a drug. It was asked which deep-sea proteins stay folded where every surface protein collapses.

> SCAN - every sequenced organism from below 3,000 metres, proteins only, no habitat labels
> FOLD - each protein modelled at trench pressure instead of at lab conditions
> HOLD - anything that keeps its shape under that load gets separated from the rest
> STRESS - the survivors run again with cold and salt added on top of the pressure
> USE - what is left matched to the industrial jobs where enzymes currently fail

Most deep-sea proteins are unremarkable. Life down there mostly solved the problem by being slow, not by being tough.

A small group did something else. They hold water in a lattice that pressure tightens rather than crushes.

That is the opposite of how a surface enzyme works. Ours rely on flexibility, and flexibility is the first thing pressure takes away.

One family stayed active across a range where standard enzymes lose all function. Cold, salt and pressure together.

That combination is exactly what industrial processes fight. Most run hot because the catalyst cannot survive anything else.

Nothing here is a product. It is a shortlist of proteins worth expressing, drawn from organisms nobody can culture.

The ocean below 3,000 metres is the largest habitat on the planet, and almost none of its chemistry has been read.

The full shortlist and what each protein could replace are laid out underneath.

hits.name: Gipp
hits.text:
jev + picsart turned one prompt into a creative system that decides before it spends

instead of letting expensive models guess their way through every step, i split the workflow in two: Jev handles the cheap decisions, Picsart handles the actual generation.

here’s exactly how i wired it:

step 1 → the brief enters once. every image, clip, audio pass and edit inherits the same campaign direction instead of starting from a blank prompt.

step 2 → Jev sits before the expensive work. it decides whether the next stage should run, stop, reuse something finished, or wait for me.

step 3 → the decision set stays tiny: allow_subagent, ask_human, stop_retry, reuse_cache. cheap calls first, expensive generation second.

step 4 → Picsart takes over the creative layer. 188 models from 34 providers sit behind the graph for image, video, audio and editing.

step 5 → every job gets its own stage. one model does not have to carry the brief, image, motion, sound and final polish by itself.

step 6 → when review rejects one output, Jev does not blindly request v2, v3, v4. it can stop the retry and change the route first.

step 7 → approved work stays alive. reuse_cache can keep 5 finished stages untouched while only the 1 broken branch gets another run.

step 8 → human review only appears where judgment matters. i am not approving every tiny action, just the decisions where taste can change the result.

step 9 → the cost gap is the fun part: 11 Jev decisions cost $0.0011 here, versus roughly $0.33 through the heavier LLM decision loop.

step 10 → once the graph works, the next campaign is not another rebuild. swap the brief, keep the logic, and run the same system again.

jev decides what deserves compute. picsart turns that decision into the asset.
